n25e1a88f740.s:
Consider the following statements about the limitations of the Green Revolution in India:
1. It led to groundwater depletion and salinity.
2. Pulses, oilseeds and millets were neglected.
3. Its gains were equally distributed among all landholders.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n25e1a88f740.x: Groundwater depletion, salinity and the neglect of pulses, oilseeds and millets were recognised limitations. Statement 3 is wrong: big landowners benefited most.

n1379927ad5b.s: Which of the following pairs (local name of shifting cultivation – region) is correctly matched?
n1379927ad5b.x: Podu is the shifting cultivation of Andhra Pradesh. Milpa belongs to Mexico (Bastar has Dipa), Kumari to the Western Ghats and Bewar to Madhya Pradesh.

n50e714cabc7.s:
Consider the following statements about the Dalhan Aatmanirbharta Mission:
1. It was announced in October 2025.
2. It provides 100% MSP procurement of tur, urad and masoor.
3. The procurement assurance is for four years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n50e714cabc7.x: Announced in October 2025, the mission provides 100% MSP procurement of tur, urad and masoor for four years, so all three statements are correct.

n8fe1d0bd0fa.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the cultivation of cotton?
o: It needs a temperature of about 21–37°C
It grows best on the laterite soil of the Western Ghats
Black or regur soil is particularly suitable for it
It is mainly a kharif crop
n8fe1d0bd0fa.x: Cotton is suited to black (regur) soil, not laterite; laterite of the Western Ghats is linked to rubber. The other statements are correct.

n41ae993960e.s: Which of the following pairs (sugarcane belt – favourable factor) is correctly matched?
o: Uttar Pradesh–Bihar – Predominance of shifting cultivation
Uttar Pradesh–Bihar – Scarcity of alluvial soil
Uttar Pradesh–Bihar – Fertile alluvium rich in lime and potash
n41ae993960e.x: The northern sugarcane concentration rests on fertile alluvium rich in lime and potash, level land, dense markets and compact cane blocks; western Uttar Pradesh is the main sugar-mill belt.

n936c4d9f545.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Kinnaur temperate apple belt – Himachal Pradesh
Largest true potato seed producer – Tripura
Second in mango production – Andhra Pradesh
n936c4d9f545.x: Lakadong turmeric comes from Meghalaya, not Tripura. The other three pairs are correct.

n31067776072.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the growth of livestock and fisheries during FY15–FY24?
o: Livestock GVA grew by about 195 percent
Livestock and fisheries grew at identical rates of 8.8 percent
Livestock grew at about 7.1 percent over the decade
Fisheries grew at about 8.8 percent over the decade
n31067776072.x: The rates were not identical: livestock grew about 7.1 percent and fisheries about 8.8 percent. Livestock GVA did grow about 195 percent.

nf588ac4287e.s: In the life cycle of a honey bee, which stage comes immediately after the larva?
nf588ac4287e.x: Honey bees pass through egg, larva, pupa and adult, so the pupa follows the larva.

new.s: Which body identified 20 agro-ecological zones in India?
new.x: The 20 agro-ecological zones are the work of the National Bureau of Soil Survey; the Planning Commission drew 15 agro-climatic zones.

new.s: The four macro agricultural regions of India were proposed by:
new.x: Sengupta and Sdasyuk divided India into four macro agricultural regions.

new.s: The 15 agro-climatic zones of the Planning Commission (Seventh Plan) are divided into how many sub-zones?
new.x: The Seventh Plan scheme has 15 agro-climatic zones and 72 sub-zones.

new.s: Which agro-climatic region, covering Punjab, Haryana and Delhi, has the highest agricultural productivity?
new.x: The Trans-Gangetic region (Punjab, Haryana, Delhi) grows wheat and rice and has the highest productivity.

new.s: The National Rice Research Institute (NRRI) is located at:
new.x: NRRI is at Cuttack; the Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR) is at Hyderabad.

new.s: Millets are promoted in India under the brand name:
new.x: India brands millets as Shree Anna.

new.s: Which year was observed as the UN International Year of Millets, pushed by India?
new.x: 2023 was the UN International Year of Millets, at India's initiative.

new.s: Which of the following is a minor millet?
new.x: Kodo (kodon) is a minor millet; bajra, jowar and ragi are the major millets.

new.s: Growing a crop from the regrowth of the stubble of the previous crop is called:
new.x: Ratoon is regrowth from stubble; relay cropping sows the next crop into the standing crop.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about cropping systems:
1. In intercropping, crops are grown together in definite rows.
2. In mixed cropping, seeds are mixed and sown with no row pattern.
3. Maize with green gram is an example of relay cropping.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Intercropping uses rows and mixed cropping has no row pattern. Maize with green gram is parallel cropping, not relay cropping.

new.s: The cropping intensity of Andhra Pradesh rose to about ____ in 2024-25.
new.x: AP's cropping intensity rose from 1.21 (2023-24) to 1.88 (2024-25).

new.s: India has the world's second-largest arable land after:
new.x: India's arable land is second only to the USA and is more than China's.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about irrigation in India?
o: India has the world's largest irrigated area
Wells and tube wells provide over 63% of irrigation
About 60% of agricultural land is irrigated
Drip and sprinkler cover only about 12% of irrigated area
new.x: Only about 56.4% of net sown area is irrigated, so 'about 60% irrigated' is incorrect.

new.s: Since which year has India been the world's largest rice exporter?
new.x: India has been the largest rice exporter since 2014-15, with about 40% of world trade.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about wheat in India:
1. It needs bright, warm sunshine at ripening.
2. The black soil of the Deccan is not suitable for wheat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Wheat needs bright warm sun at ripening. Statement 2 is wrong: wheat grows on the black soil of the Deccan as well as on Ganga-Satluj alluvium.

new.s: Which of the following pulses is a kharif crop?
new.x: Moong is a kharif pulse; gram, masoor and peas are rabi crops.

new.s: Aman rice, sown in June-July, is harvested in:
new.x: Aman rice is sown in June-July and harvested in November-December.

new.s: 'Fazenda' refers to:
new.x: Fazenda is a Brazilian plantation, not shifting cultivation; Brazil's shifting cultivation is Roca.

new.s: 'Pamlou' is the local name for shifting cultivation in:
new.x: Pamlou is practised in Manipur; Odisha has Pondu and Kerala has Poonam.

new.s: In Kerala, shifting cultivation is locally called:
new.x: Poonam (Ponam) is Kerala's name; Podu is AP, Bewar is MP and Jhum is the North-East.

new.s: BGREI (Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India) is centred on which cropping system?
new.x: BGREI, launched in 2010-11 under RKVY, targets the rice-based (rice-wheat) system of eastern States.

new.s: In which year were nutri-cereals added to the National Food Security Mission?
new.x: Nutri-cereals were added in 2018-19; coarse cereals and commercial crops came in 2014-15.

new.s: Who coined the term 'Green Revolution' in 1968?
new.x: William Gaud coined the term in 1968.

new.s: Which Union Agriculture Minister backed the Green Revolution in India?
new.x: C. Subramaniam was the Union Agriculture Minister who backed it; B.P. Pal was the first DG of ICAR.

new.s: In its first stage, the Green Revolution spread mainly in:
o: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
new.x: The first stage covered Punjab, Haryana and western UP; the eastern belt lagged.

new.s: Which State is India's leading producer of bajra?
new.x: Bajra production order is Rajasthan > UP > Haryana.

new.s: Which State is the leading producer of ragi in India?
new.x: Karnataka leads in ragi.

new.s: In 2024-25, which State ranked second in rice production in India?
new.x: The 2024-25 order was UP (20.76 MT) > Telangana (17.45) > West Bengal (16.02) > Punjab (14.36).

new.s: The Spices Board is headquartered at:
new.x: The Spices Board is at Kochi; the Rubber Board is at Kottayam.

new.s: Which commodity board has its headquarters in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: The Tobacco Board is at Guntur, the only board seated in AP.

new.s: How many statutory commodity boards function under the Ministry of Commerce?
new.x: Five statutory boards are under Commerce: tea, coffee, rubber, spices and tobacco.

new.s: The National Jute Board is headquartered at:
new.x: The National Jute Board, under the Ministry of Textiles, is at Kolkata.

new.s: Jute-ICARE stands for:
o: Integrated Crop and Agricultural Research Enterprise
Improved Cultivation and Advanced Retting Exercise
Improved Crop Assessment and Retting Evaluation
new.x: Jute-ICARE is Improved Cultivation and Advanced Retting Exercise, with certified seed and the SONA retting consortium.

new.s: SONA, promoted under Jute-ICARE, is a:
new.x: SONA is a microbial retting consortium; the app for jute farmers is Paat-Mitro.

new.s: Which oilseed is grown in both kharif and rabi seasons?
new.x: Sunflower is grown in both seasons; mustard and linseed are rabi, groundnut kharif.

new.s: Which of the following is a kharif oilseed?
new.x: Sesamum is a kharif oilseed; linseed, safflower and rapeseed are rabi oilseeds.

new.s: Which State leads India in rapeseed-mustard production?
new.x: Rajasthan produces about 45-49% of rapeseed-mustard.

new.s: Which crop is called 'vegetable meat'?
new.x: Soybean is called vegetable meat.

new.s: Which State leads India in oil palm area, production and productivity?
new.x: Andhra Pradesh leads oil palm on all three counts.

new.s: 'Golden Fibre' refers to:
new.x: Jute is the Golden Fibre; cotton is the Silver Fibre.

new.s: The Silver Fibre Revolution relates to:
new.x: Silver Fibre is cotton, linked to the Technology Mission on Cotton.

new.s: The Golden Revolution is related to:
new.x: The Golden Revolution is horticulture and honey; oilseeds are the Yellow Revolution.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh ranks first in India in the production of:
new.x: AP is 1st in chillies and 2nd in turmeric; Gujarat now leads tobacco.

new.s: Which town of Andhra Pradesh is the chilli-trade hub and seat of the Tobacco Board?
new.x: Guntur is the chilli-trade hub and the seat of the Tobacco Board.

new.s: In 2024-25, which State led India in tobacco production?
Which country is the world's largest producer of tea?
new.x: China leads world tea output; India is 2nd.

new.s: What is India's rank in world natural rubber production (FAO 2024)?
new.x: India is 6th (5th earlier); Thailand leads.

new.s: India's rank in world coffee production is:
new.x: India is 7th; Brazil and Vietnam lead.

new.s: Rubber requires an annual rainfall of over:
new.x: Rubber needs over 200 cm of rain, not 100 cm.

new.s: The sugarcane crushing season in the sub-tropical belt of north India runs from:
new.x: The sub-tropical crushing season is November to February; the tropical belt's is October to May/June.

new.s: The Dooars region is known for which plantation crop?
new.x: Darjeeling and the Dooars in West Bengal are tea areas.

new.s: The Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (CPCRI) is located at:
new.x: CPCRI is at Kasaragod.

new.s: The Indian Institute of Spices Research is located at:
new.x: IISR (spices) is at Kozhikode; the other IISR (sugarcane) is at Lucknow.

new.s: Colonial plantations of tea, coffee, rubber and indigo in India were mainly:
new.x: Colonial plantations were European-dominated and export-oriented.

new.s: The Grey Revolution is related to:
new.x: The Grey Revolution relates to fertilisers.

new.s: The Silver Revolution is related to:
new.x: Silver Revolution is eggs and poultry; Silver Fibre is cotton.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (revolution – sector) is correctly matched?
o: Pink Revolution – Onion and meat export
new.x: Pink is onion and meat export. Yellow is oilseeds, Golden is horticulture and Blue is fish.

new.s: Punganur, a dwarf cattle breed, is native to which district of Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Punganur is from Chittoor; Ongole is from Prakasam.

new.s: Murrah is a breed of:
new.x: Murrah is a buffalo breed of Haryana.

new.s: Kadaknath, a poultry breed with black meat, is native to:
new.x: Kadaknath comes from Jhabua, Madhya Pradesh.

new.s: The Jamunapari goat comes from which State?
new.x: Jamunapari is a goat of Etawah, Uttar Pradesh.

new.s: Hallikar is a draught cattle breed of:
new.x: Hallikar is a Karnataka draught breed.

new.s: As per the 20th Livestock Census, India's total livestock population was about:
new.x: Total livestock was 535.78 million, up 4.6% over 2012; 302.79 million were bovines.

new.s: The 20th Livestock Census of India was conducted in:
new.x: The 20th Census was in 2019; the 21st (2024-25) is digital.

new.s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank in milk production in 2025-26?
new.x: AP was 7th in milk, 4th in meat and 1st in eggs.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's rank in meat production in 2025-26 was:
new.x: AP was 4th in meat (5th in 2023-24).

new.s: Which is Andhra Pradesh's leading milk-producing district?
new.x: Chittoor is AP's leading dairy district.

new.s: What is India's rank in world egg production?
new.x: India is 2nd in eggs, with 149.11 billion in 2024-25.

new.s: Operation Flood was launched in 1970 by the:
new.x: Operation Flood (1970) was run by the National Dairy Development Board.

new.s: India's per capita milk availability in 2024-25 was about:
new.x: It was 485 g/day in 2024-25, up from 471 g/day in 2023-24.

new.s: The harvest of wild fish stock is called:
new.x: Capture fishery harvests wild stock; culture (aquaculture, mariculture) is controlled farming.

new.s: Cold-water fisheries such as trout are found above an altitude of about:
new.x: Trout cold-water fisheries lie above 1,500 m.

new.s: The Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture (CIFA) is located at:
new.x: CIFA is at Bhubaneswar; CIFT and CMFRI are at Kochi.

new.s: What is India's rank in world fish production?
new.x: India is the 2nd largest fish producer.

new.s: Eri silk, known as 'peace silk', comes from silkworms feeding on:
new.x: Eri silkworms feed on castor (and tapioca); muga feeds on som and soalu.

new.s: Muga silkworms feed on:
new.x: Muga feeds on som and soalu; tasar feeds on Terminalia and sal.

new.s: Oak (temperate) tasar silk is produced mainly in:
new.x: Oak tasar comes from Manipur, Uttarakhand, HP and J&K.

new.s: Lac culture is the rearing of:
new.x: Lac culture produces lac from lac insects.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about silk in India:
1. India is the only country producing all five silks.
2. India is the largest producer of raw silk in the world.
3. Karnataka is the largest silk-producing State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: India produces all five silks and Karnataka leads. Statement 2 is wrong: India is 2nd after China.

new.s: Which State is known as the 'Orchid State' of India?
new.x: Arunachal Pradesh has the most orchid species; Sikkim is 2nd.

new.s: Which State is India's largest mango producer?
new.x: Uttar Pradesh leads in mango; AP is 2nd.

new.s: Over 50% of India's kiwi is produced in:
new.x: Arunachal Pradesh grows over half of India's kiwi.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh ranks first in India in the productivity of:
new.x: AP is 1st in cocoa productivity.

new.s: Which of the following plantation crops falls under the Ministry of Commerce?
new.x: Tea, coffee and rubber are under Commerce; coconut, arecanut, cashew, palm and cocoa under Agriculture.

new.s: How many Mega Food Parks are operational in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: AP has 3 sanctioned Mega Food Parks, of which 2 are operational.

new.s: PMFME (2020) is linked to which approach?
new.x: PMFME, under Aatmanirbhar Bharat, follows One District One Product.

new.s: The APEDA Act was passed in:
new.x: The APEDA Act dates from 1985.

new.s: The Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute is located at:
new.x: Sheep and wool research is at Avikanagar, Rajasthan.

new.s: The High Security Animal Disease Laboratory is located at:
new.x: It is at Bhopal; Karnal hosts NDRI.
